title: Filtered 2-colimits of categories
statement:
Let $I$ be a preordered set (in the applications a directed one) and $(\mathcal C_i)_{i\in I}$
categories. A *cocone of categories* with vertex a category $\mathcal D$ consists of

- transition functors $T_{ij}\colon\mathcal C_i\to\mathcal C_j$ for $i\le j$,
- functors $\Phi_i\colon\mathcal C_i\to\mathcal D$, and
- natural isomorphisms $\theta_{ij}\colon\Phi_j\circ T_{ij}\cong\Phi_i$ for $i\le j$.

No coherence between the transition functors is required. The cocone *is a filtered 2-colimit*
if it satisfies:

- **(Obj)** every object of $\mathcal D$ is isomorphic to $\Phi_i(x)$ for some $i\in I$ and
  $x\in\mathcal C_i$;
- **(Hom-surj)** for all $i,j\in I$, $x\in\mathcal C_i$, $y\in\mathcal C_j$ and every morphism
  $\varphi\colon\Phi_i(x)\to\Phi_j(y)$ there are $k\ge i,j$ and a morphism
  $g\colon T_{ik}x\to T_{jk}y$ in $\mathcal C_k$ with
  $\varphi=\theta_{jk,y}\circ\Phi_k(g)\circ\theta_{ik,x}^{-1}$;
- **(Hom-inj)** for every $k\in I$ and morphisms $g,g'\colon x\to y$ in $\mathcal C_k$ with
  $\Phi_k(g)=\Phi_k(g')$ there is $k'\ge k$ with $T_{kk'}(g)=T_{kk'}(g')$.

In particular, in a filtered 2-colimit every object of $\mathcal D$ comes from a finite stage,
and morphisms of $\mathcal C_k$ identified in $\mathcal D$ are identified at a finite stage.
This is a property of ordinary categories and functors; no higher categories are involved.

proof.text: The two final assertions are (Obj) and (Hom-inj) restated.

The conditions characterise the 2-colimit. Suppose $I$ is directed and the transition functors
are coherent (a pseudofunctor $I\to\mathrm{Cat}$, with the $\theta_{ij}$ compatible with its
structure isomorphisms). The 2-colimit is then modelled by the ordinary category $\mathcal C_\infty$
whose objects are pairs $(i,x)$ with $x\in\mathcal C_i$ and whose morphisms are
$\Hom((i,x),(j,y))=\operatorname{colim}_{k\ge i,j}\Hom_{\mathcal C_k}(T_{ik}x,T_{jk}y)$, a
filtered colimit of sets, with composition defined after passing to a common index. The cocone
induces a comparison functor $\Phi\colon\mathcal C_\infty\to\mathcal D$,
$(i,x)\mapsto\Phi_i(x)$. It is essentially surjective if and only if (Obj) holds. On morphisms
it is the canonical map $\operatorname{colim}_k\Hom_{\mathcal C_k}(T_{ik}x,T_{jk}y)\to
\Hom_{\mathcal D}(\Phi_i x,\Phi_j y)$: (Hom-surj) is its surjectivity, and since the colimit is
filtered, two elements with the same image can be represented at a common index $k$, where
(Hom-inj) makes them equal at a later index; so (Hom-surj) and (Hom-inj) say that $\Phi$ is
fully faithful. Hence, under these assumptions, the cocone is a filtered 2-colimit if and only if
$\Phi$ is an equivalence of categories.
